title: How to Make Slowed and Reverb Songs – Free Guide
description: Learn how to make slowed and reverb music free in your browser: load a track, apply speed, reverb and bass, then export a WAV or MP3. No signup, no watermark.
h1: How to Make Slowed and Reverb
heroText: Slowed and reverb means lowering a song's speed and pitch while adding a reverb effect, so it plays back slower, deeper and dreamier than the original. You can do it free in your browser with [Slowed and Reverb Maker](/): load an MP3 or WAV, pick the Classic Slowed + Reverb preset, trim the section you want on the waveform, and export the result as WAV or MP3. No signup, no software install, and your audio never leaves your device.

sections.title: The Short Answer
sections.body: To make a slowed and reverb edit of a song, you slow it down to roughly 0.8x of its original speed, drop the pitch a step or two so voices stay natural, add a wet reverb effect around half mix, and often lift the bass slightly for warmth. The finished edit is the deep, atmospheric version popular on TikTok and YouTube lo-fi playlists. Here is the exact process, start to export, using a free [audio editor online](/) that runs the whole job in your browser. The three numbers to remember are 0.8x speed, 50% reverb and 20% bass. Start there, listen to one verse, and adjust only the setting that feels wrong rather than changing everything at once.

sections.title: Step by Step
sections.body: The whole edit takes about two minutes once you have your audio file saved on your device. Every step runs locally, so nothing is uploaded to a server and there is no account to create.

steps.title: Save the song as an audio file
steps.body: Find the MP3, WAV, M4A, OGG or FLAC file of the track you want to edit. Slowed and Reverb Maker loads these formats directly from your device and renders the song as a playable waveform, so you can see exactly where the intro, drop and outro sit before you change anything.

steps.title: Load it into the browser tool
steps.body: Open [Slowed and Reverb Maker](/) and load your file. The waveform appears immediately and the original plays back so you have a reference. Because processing happens in your browser, a five-minute song is ready in seconds and stays private to your device.

steps.title: Pick the Classic Slowed + Reverb preset
steps.body: The preset sets speed to 0.8x, adds a 50% reverb mix and a 20% bass boost with pitch unchanged. This is the sound most people mean when they say slowed and reverb. If your song already sounds dark and bass-heavy, drop the bass boost to about 10% so vocals stay clear.

steps.title: Fine-tune speed and pitch
steps.body: Listen to the first verse at 0.8x. If it drags, try 0.85x; if you want the classic deep feel, go to 0.75x. Small pitch changes of about -1 to -2 semitones keep voices believable while deepening the tone. For a faster, brighter take on the same song, the [nightcore maker](/nightcore-maker/) applies the sped up version instead.

steps.title: Trim to the section you want
steps.body: Use the waveform trim handles to cut the track down to the 30-60 second hook you plan to post. A clean trim at the end of a phrase sounds better than a hard cut mid-word, so zoom in on the waveform and set the end point where the line finishes.

steps.title: Preview, then export WAV or MP3
steps.body: Play the trimmed section once more to check the reverb tail does not clip the ending. Then render the adjusted audio offline and export it as WAV for full quality or MP3 for a smaller file that uploads fast to TikTok, Instagram or YouTube. The export matches what you heard in the preview exactly.

sections.title: The Settings Explained
sections.body: Four numbers shape the slowed and reverb sound. You do not need to understand signal processing to use them, but knowing what each one does helps you fix a mix that feels off instead of guessing.

items.title: Speed
items.body: Speed multiplies playback rate. At 0.8x a three-minute song runs about 3:45 and every pitch drops with it, which is why slowed tracks sound deeper. Below 0.7x most vocals become muddy and the beat loses its groove, so 0.75x is the practical floor for rap or dance tracks.

items.title: Pitch
items.body: Pitch shift changes note height without changing tempo. Slowing a song already lowers pitch, so only nudge it a semitone or two. Positive pitch with slow speed gives the daycore feel, and it also rescues songs whose vocals sound too deep after heavy slowing.

items.title: Reverb effect
items.body: Reverb simulates the sound bouncing around a large room, adding a soft tail after each note. Around 50% mix is the classic range: clearly audible space without drowning the vocals. Push toward 70% for a dreamy, distant feel, and reduce it if consonants start smearing together.

items.title: Bass boost
items.body: Bass boost raises the low end so the slower track keeps weight on small phone speakers. 20% suits most songs; hip-hop and EDM tracks often need less because they already carry heavy low frequencies. On laptop or phone playback, check that the boost does not rattle the verse.

faq.question: What speed is a slowed and reverb song?
faq.answer: Most slowed and reverb edits sit between 0.75x and 0.85x of the original speed, with 0.8x the common default. At 0.8x, a three-minute song lasts roughly 3 minutes 45 seconds, and the pitch drops with it automatically, giving the deeper tone listeners expect from the style.

faq.question: How much reverb should I add?
faq.answer: Start at a 50% reverb mix, which is what the Classic Slowed + Reverb preset uses. That level gives a clear room sound without burying the vocals. If the song is sparse, like an acoustic or piano track, you can go to 65-70% for a dreamier feel; dense mixes usually need less.

faq.question: Can I make slowed and reverb on my phone?
faq.answer: Yes. The tool is a browser-based audio editor online, so it works in a mobile browser with no app install. Load the file from your phone storage, apply the preset, trim the waveform, and export MP3. The processing runs on your device, so it also works offline once the page has loaded.

faq.question: Does slowing a song change the pitch?
faq.answer: It does, and that is part of the sound. Reducing playback speed lowers pitch proportionally: 0.8x speed drops every note by roughly a third of a tone. If you want slower tempo with the original pitch, raise the pitch control back up after slowing, which is how daycore edits stay true to the vocal.

faq.question: What format should I export?
faq.answer: Export WAV when you want full, lossless quality, for example as a source file for a video edit. Export MP3 when the file is going straight to social media, because it is much smaller and uploads faster. Both exports are rendered offline and match the preview you heard exactly.

faq.question: How is slowed and reverb different from nightcore?
faq.answer: They are opposite directions on the same dial. Nightcore speeds a song up to around 1.25x, raising the pitch for a bright, energetic sped up version. Slowed and reverb reduces speed toward 0.8x and adds a reverb effect for a deep, relaxed feel. The [full comparison](/slowed-vs-nightcore/) breaks down when to use each.
